problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039044/assets/0d278fe1bf34cd60877be6886c90e1734fab7433f9f94ad7765d379e69c2da42.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(2,2),$ and passes through the point $(4,6).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(2,2),$ and so we have

$$
x-2=p{t}^{2},\,y-2=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(4,6),$ we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=6$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}2=p{t}^{2} \\ 4=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ 2 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ 2 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-2=(2){t}^{2},\,y-2=2(2)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-2=2{t}^{2},\,y-2=4t.
$$

Question 1
?

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the parabola shown above?

a
x+2=12t2,y+2=t
b
x−2=2t2,y−2=4t
c
x+2=2t2,y+2=4t
d
x−2=12t2,y−2=t
e
x−2=2t2,y−2=2t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at (2,2), and passes through the point (4,6).

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at (h,k) are

x−h=pt2,y−k=2pt,

where p is constant.

In our case, (h,k)=(2,2), and so we have

x−2=pt2,y−2=2pt.

Since the parabola passes through (4,6), we can substitute x=4 and y=6 into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

{2=pt24=2pt.

Solving the second equation for t, we have

4=2pt2=ptt=2p.

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for p, we get

2=p(2p)22=p⋅4p22=4pp=2.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x−2=(2)t2,y−2=2(2)t,

which simplify to

x−2=2t2,y−2=4t.
